newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine carmakers see higher 1997 output/exports.
newsitem.headline: Argentine carmakers see higher 1997 output/exports.

text.p: Argentine carmakers expect to increase output and exports in 1997, regaining ground lost during two years of a steep fall amid recession.

"We are confident our market share will grow ... and we will push ahead with a very ambitious export plan," Jorge Mostany, President of the local unit of Ford Motor Co said in a survey conducted by newspaper El Cronista.

Manuel Antelo, President of CIADEA, licensee of Renault SA, said: "for the 1996-2001 the company will invest about $500 million to increase competitiveness, revamping its plant and developing new products."
"In 1997 CIADEA plans to reaffirm its leadership in the local market and to widen its presence in regional ones."
Francisco Macri, President of Sevel, licensee of France's Peugeot SA, said: "We aim to consolidate our position in the market, to incorporate new products both imported and locally made."
Macri warned that for the industry expansion it is vital "to defend free access of Argentine products to Mercosur," the customs union between Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay.
"This year will end with a slight increase of sales and a significative increase in profitability," he said.

Norbeto Dubar, head of the local unit of Germany's Volkswagen AG, said that "next year Volkswagen will complete investments planned for 1995/97 and will look forward to consolidate its growth of the last 20 months."

After the split of Autolatina, a joint venture between Ford and Volkswagen in Argentina and Brazil, Volkswagen ranked first in Argentine car production in September with almost 8,000 of the 28,000 vehicles made.
Ford, CIADEA, Sevel and Volkswagen accounted for almost 90 percent of the 223,000 vehicles produced in Argentina in the first nine months of the year.

Under protective government policies, the Argentine car sector boomed from 1991 and made a record 400,000 vehicles in 1994; but then it was hit by a recession induced by the Mexican peso devaluation at the end of that year and in 1995 production fell to 283,000 cars.
Ford's Mostany said he foresees total sales of Argentine carmakers will be about 400,000 units in 1997.
